pr.title: Sign off on the newest verdict and drop the multi-verdict header
pr.head: aca378540beac9fdad3ce41943b0a00a54644b71

summary: Projector's review loops can run on several models at once, such as one loop in Claude Code and one in Codex, each posting reviews as the same GitHub account. On your own pull request, Projector cannot post an approval or a change request, so it uses draft state as the sign-off: draft means the head still needs changes, ready means a review found it clean. This pull request changes how that sign-off is decided when several models review one head.

Before this change (from #239), a head was signed off only when every model with a verdict on it was clean, no model was still reviewing it, and no finding thread was open, and publish waited up to review.peer_wait seconds for a model that had reviewed an earlier head. That broke when one model's loop was stopped partway: its last change request held the pull request in draft. Now the newest verdict wins: after each self-review publish, publish reads the Projector verdicts on the head and sets draft state by the newest one, whichever model gave it.

• Sign-off. publish drops the peer wait and the every-model rule, and project review status prints the newest verdict, each model's newest verdict, and the open finding threads.
  • Accounts. Verdicts count from the reviewer's account and from any account that owns the repository, belongs to its organization, or collaborates on it, the same rule the site uses, so fix-pr runs status once instead of once per account.
  • Site. The summary header goes back to one status chip linked to the newest review, restoring the front end to its state before #233.
  • Plan. The plan gains § 9, which records the decision and marks the old rule and the adoption design superseded. It stays in-progress until a two-host run is done.

cards.title: What the review found
cards.html: The latest head is clean. The first review found that two models publishing within the same second or two could leave the pull request ready with a finding open, because publish counted open threads only before it submitted. This head re-reads the census in the draft step and keeps the pull request a draft while any finding thread is open, whatever the newest verdict. It also merges main and has the site read TRUSTED from review.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Verdict: a Projector review's clean or changes-requested result, recorded in a marker comment that also names the head and the model.
  • Self-review: a review of a pull request the reviewer account wrote, where GitHub allows only a COMMENT review.
  • Finding thread: an inline review thread opened by a Projector review for a P1 or P2 finding.
  • Census: the count of Projector finding threads, open and resolved, that a verdict rests on.

groups.title: The newest verdict sets draft state
groups.kicker: How publish and status decide the sign-off now
intro: After it submits a self-review, publish lists the pull request's Projector reviews, adds the review it just posted in case the listing lags, and takes the newest verdict on the head by submission time and then review id. Draft state follows it: draft for changes-requested, ready for clean, unless a Projector finding thread is open, which keeps the pull request a draft whatever the newest verdict says. When another model posted between this review's submit and its draft step, publish prints that newer verdict.

The removed code is the every-model rule: models_on, signoff, pending_peers, sign with its polling wait, and the review.peer_wait setting. The new verdicts lists reviews from the reviewer's account and from trusted repository accounts, and newest_verdicts keeps each model's newest verdict on a head, newest first.

checks.text: A clean verdict needs every Projector finding thread settled when its review counts them, and the draft step counts them again after submitting, because another model can post a finding in between.

files.note: Replaces the every-model sign-off with verdicts and newest_verdicts, and sets draft state in publish from the newest verdict and the open finding threads.

checks.text: The draft step re-reads census and keeps a draft while any finding is open. The review reran its reproduction, in which another model posts a finding between this review's census and its submit; the pull request now ends a draft with one open thread.

A cross-author review posts APPROVE only for a clean verdict where review.allow_approve is true, REQUEST_CHANGES for changes requested, and COMMENT otherwise; the review traced each branch and the full suite passes.

files.note: Stops reading review.peer_wait and prints the newest verdict when another model's decided the draft state.

groups.title: One status per head on the site
groups.kicker: The summary header and Reviews row go back to a single chip
intro: The site showed a head reviewed by several models as a button with an asterisk and a hover card of each model's verdict. That card existed to explain the every-model rule. Under the newest-verdict rule, the header shows the one status the newest review gave, linked to that review, as it did before #233.

The front-end files are restored byte for byte to their state before #233. One part of #233 stays: an incremental review's "incremental from" link names its own model's full review of the earlier head, never another model's.

checks.text: The review ran npm ci, npm run check, and npm run build in site/, and the build left the tree clean. After the merge with main, this pull request's changed lines under site/src match the first head's, so #242's sidebar work is kept.

files.note: review_statuses keeps each head's newest review, whichever model wrote it, and reads TRUSTED from review.
Removes the multi-model button and its event wiring; statusHtml draws one link.

groups.title: Skills and CLI docs describe the newest-verdict rule
groups.kicker: What review and fix loops now read and report
intro: review-pr now says the newest verdict on a head signs it off and that nothing waits. fix-pr runs project review status once, because status reads every account the repository lets in. The loop skills drop the sign-off from what a subagent reports and add the newer verdict when publish names one.

groups.title: The plan records the decision
intro: The multi-model-review plan appends § 9, "The newest verdict wins", with the rule, the status output, and the rejected alternatives. § 2.3 and § 2.8 and the superseded acceptance criteria stay as short stubs, so no cited number moves. The plan stays in-progress because criterion 15, a Claude Code loop and a Codex loop run by hand, needs two hosts.

files.note: Read § 9 for the decision and its rejected alternatives.
